newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's SFE to study SPI close distortion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's SFE to study SPI close distortion.

text.p: The Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) said on Monday it would undertake an analysis of the mechanism for calculating the settlement price of its Share Price Index (SPI) futures after concerns it could be distorted by late share trading designed to manipulate the closing prices of stocks.
The SFE said the decision followed discussions with the Australian Securities Commission (ASC).

"The ASC's concerns have arisen in the course of its investigation into trading in shares on the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) and SPI futures contracts on SFE on the last day of the March quarter this year," the SFE said in a statement.
The SFE said the ASC had not formed any conclusions as to whether any trading which took place that day breached the law.

"SFE has agreed to analyse the settlement mechanism to determine whether it is the most appropriate mechanism for the Australian market, and to ascertain the relative strengths and weaknesses of any alternate mechanisms which may be available," the SFE said.

Under the SFE's current rules, the SPI settlement price, which is calculated at the close of trading on the last trading day of each quarter, is based on the closing quotation of the All Ordinaries index on the ASX.

"The ASC will also assess whether the current settlement mechanism presents significant financial risk to legitimate arbitrage traders on expiry of the SPI futures contract at the end of each quarter which might act as a disincentive to arbitrage trading," the SFE said.
The SFE said it expected its analysis to be completed this year.
